convoLines.text: "About whatever's been weighing on me — Do you ever — no. Never mind." They don't look away, though. They want you to ask.
"So I had this idea — Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that."
They lean back on their hands. "Wind's up tonight. Good night to not be walking."
"I can breathe all the way down again. I couldn't, before you sat down."
"This one — Bamboo Shoot. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Good question." "My well's dry on that one. Ask me tomorrow — maybe I'll have dreamed something."
"Joy is a resource. I'm foraging for it. Some days the yield is terrible."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on wanting to laugh again, properly."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"My cut needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
Quiet for a long time. Then, barely audible: "I took 1× Stone. I won't do it again."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"What got you through the first week? The very first days."
"Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time."
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
"Still on that wound care."
"Alright. Catch you later."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the funniest thing you've seen — Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it. Trust me. Mostly."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on the funniest thing you've seen."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "I dreamed Jamal was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I wake before anyone else. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the ghost pipe patch past the treeline."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the ghost pipe patch past the treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.

A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to understand what happened. I keep my head down. Old habit. It kept me alive before; it keeps me alive now." Quiet. Real.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
"Still on that foraging help."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About whether they can trust you — Can I trust you? I mean really. Just... be straight with me."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast. Seen worse."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on whether they can trust you."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Give it time."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I talk to both sides. It hasn't exploded yet."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Jackfruit — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never did finish talking about that wound care — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'Alright. Catch you later.'"

"It's my best friend, Belay. Was taken at the Scattering. We had plans. Stupid, small, beautiful plans. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Right. Right."
"Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I clean up other people's messes quietly when the fire gets loud. Everyone's got a tell. That's mine."
"Someone has to say the thing nobody's saying. Probably won't be me."
"Still on what's been happening. You know?"
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Relax — the soup is fine. Mostly fine. Try it and find out."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"Here. I made an extra." Isaac presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Watch for this: The hissing stops. Ducks in a row, every time. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
"Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane… That's Nevermore telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. I know the far treeline, past the rocks — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "That's the whole of it. The director's cut adds nothing."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"The world took a lot. It's not getting my sense of humor."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Hey — I found some Wood Sorrel today. You were right, it was right where you said. — ask anyone!"
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson. Thank you. Really."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them Spicebush — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Jesse — Gauntlet, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
"Still nothing on Belay. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took you — The Quiet Room, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"As I said — Still on what's been happening. ...anyway, where was I."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"When's the last time you really laughed?"
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it."
"I believe in breakfast. In people showing up. Small, provable things. The big beliefs all broke — the small ones held."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what you believe in."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Anyway, that's me."
"That again?" Jesse sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that foraging help."
"About that question — I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
The conversation cools to something businesslike.
"Still on what you think happened to us."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Meera always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
A long exhale. "I'll get there. Just needed a minute where I didn't have to be fine."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.

"I wasn't a hotel housekeeper. I was a librarian. You looked at me like I mattered, and I wanted to keep that. So I gave you someone worth looking at. That person isn't real. This one is — and it's worse, isn't it?"
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to keep the peace. I wanted an edge. You were new, you were listening, and I used it. I'm not proud of that."
"We went over this," Yuki says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
Yuki looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Yuki rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"Since Meera died... I keep expecting to see Meera at the fire. Stupid."
"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"The cistern's nearly dry — 4 liters left. I need someone to haul water with me at first light. Two of us, half the trips. Will you come?"
"Do the math with me: 4 liters, 9 people. That's not tomorrow's water. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
As I said — Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The Exchange. They just... took Ella and Yuki. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 12 days back. Still on your mind? 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.' We still owe grief a proper ending, too."
Yuki has an edge today — something curdled.
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Good question." Arguments cost calories. I do the math out loud until people stop.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"I've talked down fights before. It's a skill. A tiring one."
"I don't pick sides. I pick the group. Every time."
"Still on wanting to keep the peace."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took me. The Exchange — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

deathBeat: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Jamal Adamczyk is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: 🕯️ Jamal Adamczyk is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Jamal — and Jamal is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d43: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. The Loud Beast is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d43: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Big Loud is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d43: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. The Paparazzo is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
recoverHome: d42: That night, they bring Jamal home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d41: At the grave, Isaac, Meera, Jesse speak for Alex — "Jamal trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d41: SYSTEM: You know this plant the way it knows itself. Concerning. Impressive.
